name: Precision friction calorimeter
summary: Joule's paddle-wheel apparatus, driven by falling weights and read with finely calibrated thermometers, measured the heat produced by friction with careful corrections for losses.
description: Falling weights drove paddle wheels in calorimetric vessels. Dancer and Fastré thermometers, calibrated using Regnault’s method, measured small rises; separate trials estimated heat leakage, apparatus heat capacity, pulley friction and residual motion.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: Joule's earlier estimates scattered widely, so he built an apparatus that let heat leakage, apparatus heat capacity and friction losses be measured and corrected.
